outcome: No accepted resolution, and no in-window (since 26 January 2024) public argument that settles the conjecture or any of its cases, has been found. The only full claim, arXiv:2011.05544 (Yousefzadehfard, November 2020, before the window), was withdrawn in v2 by its author with a note that 'There is a problem with the Theorem 4.7'; the 2023 Gregory preprint still calls the conjecture 'wide open'. No AI system is named in any source on this problem.
problem_asks: (a) For every smooth projective variety X over every finite field F_q, of any dimension. (b) For every higher algebraic K-group K_i(X), for every degree i >= 1. (c) The claim that each such group vanishes up to torsion, i.e. K_i(X) tensored with Q is zero (equivalently, K_i(X) is torsion). The statement is one universal claim over varieties, degrees and fields; it is also called the Beilinson-Parshin conjecture. Settling only a dimension, a class of varieties, or a single degree would settle part of (a) or (b), not the whole.

events.what_happened: Aydin Yousefzadehfard posted 'Proof of the Parshin's Conjecture' (arXiv:2011.05544, primary math.KT, 11 pages). The v1 abstract opens 'We prove the Parshin's conjecture' and claims rational triviality of higher algebraic K-theory of smooth projective varieties over finite fields, with the consequence that for a field of positive characteristic p and n > 0 the only rationally non-trivial weight in K_n(F) tensor Q is n (a Beilinson-Soule-type statement). The author withdrew v2 (21 Nov 2020, 1 KB). The arXiv record shows the note 'This paper has been withdrawn by Aydin Yousefzadehfard' and the comment 'There is a problem with the Theorem 4.7.' The fetched record also reportedly says the problem could be fixed with double duals but that this would undermine the construction (this last clause is the fetching tool's paraphrase, not verbatim). The v1 outline (Introduction; Binary Complexes; Grayson Filtration; Proof of the main theorem; a fibration with rationally trivial fibre and base) comes from search snippets; I could not read the PDF body.
events.revisions: v1 11 Nov 2020 (13 KB, 11 pages, 'Comments are welcome'); v2 21 Nov 2020 (1 KB), withdrawn by the author. No later version found.
events.delivers: Claims the conjecture as stated: for every smooth projective variety X over a finite field, K_i(X) tensor Q = 0 for all i >= 1, with no restriction on dimension, field or degree in the abstract. Claim exists only in v1; the withdrawn v2 has no content.
events.remains: Nothing if v1 is correct. But the v1 argument is not established on the record: the author has withdrawn the later version and has flagged Theorem 4.7 as problematic. I could not check whether Theorem 4.7 is a step in v1's main argument.
events.time_since_posted: about 71 months (5 years 11 months) as of 13 Oct 2026; no public engagement with the argument found
events.doubts: (1) The author's own withdrawal of v2 and the comment 'There is a problem with the Theorem 4.7.' on the arXiv record (abstract page of v2, fetched 13 Oct 2026). (2) The withdrawal left v1 publicly available; v1's body could not be read by my tools, so I cannot say whether the flagged step is in v1. (3) Oliver Gregory's 2023 preprint (arXiv:2302.09867) states the conjecture 'remains wide open'; the bibliography of that preprint, read in full on 13 Oct 2026, contains no entry for arXiv:2011.05544 or for this author. (4) No journal publication, refutation, expert note, MathSciNet or zbMATH review was found (zbMATH/MathSciNet not accessible to me). (5) Both the v1 claim and the 'wide open' statement are in the public record; neither has been answered by the other.

withdrawn.what: v2 (submitted 21 Nov 2020, 1 KB) withdrawn. arXiv note: 'This paper has been withdrawn by Aydin Yousefzadehfard'. Record comment on Theorem 4.7 as quoted above. No explicit reason given on the page.
withdrawn.date: withdrawal date not shown; v2 submitted 2020-11-21

events.direction: Asserts the conjecture itself (rational vanishing of all higher K-groups of all smooth projective varieties over finite fields). If correct, it cuts in the conjecture's direction; no counterexample is involved.

events.what_happened: Goncalo Tabuada, 'HPD-invariance of the Tate, Beilinson and Parshin conjectures' (arXiv:1712.05397; v1 14 Dec 2017; v3 3 May 2018, whose comment says the revision uses topological periodic cyclic homology and adds results for the p-version of the Tate conjecture). Abstract: 'We prove that the Tate, Beilinson and Parshin conjectures are invariant under Homological Projective Duality'. For k = F_q the paper proves Parshin's conjecture P(X) in restricted families: linear sections of determinantal varieties (Theorem 1.8), Segre varieties (Example 1.9), the rational normal scroll S_{1,1,2} (Subexample 1.10), square matrices (Example 1.11), a surface in Z^2_{3,3} (Subexample 1.12), and intersections of two quadrics under dim L = 2 with p not 2 when d is odd (Theorem 1.14). It extends the conjectures to stacks and proves the stacky version for low-dimensional orbifolds (Corollary 1.21). The Parshin content is Theorem 1.3 (P(X) iff the noncommutative version for perf_dg(X)) and Theorem 1.4 (P(X_L) iff P(Y_L) for HP-dual linear sections). Read from the ar5iv rendering, presumably the latest version.
events.revisions: v1 14 Dec 2017; v3 3 May 2018 (adds topological periodic cyclic homology argument and p-version Tate results). v2 not checked.
events.delivers: Proves P(X) (K_i(X) tensor Q = 0 for i >= 1) for restricted families of smooth projective varieties over finite fields, namely the listed determinantal linear sections, Segre varieties, S_{1,1,2}, square-matrix sections, a particular surface, and some intersections of two quadrics (subject to the dimension and characteristic conditions in the theorems); and for stacks [X/G] with dim X <= 1 and p not dividing |G| (Corollary 1.21). Also gives the HPD-invariance equivalences.
events.remains: P for all other smooth projective varieties over finite fields, including general varieties of every dimension; the stacky statement for dim X >= 2 is only conditional (Corollary 1.21 second clause).
events.time_since_posted: about 106 months (8 years 10 months); no public engagement with the Parshin part found
events.doubts: (1) The journal version, J. Noncommut. Geom. 17 (2023), no. 1, 163-188 (DOI 10.4171/JNCG/462), is titled 'HPD-invariance of the Tate conjecture(s)'. Its published abstract mentions only the Tate conjecture and its variants, and the extension to stacks; it does not mention Beilinson or Parshin. I could not establish from the published abstract whether the Parshin cases survived into print. (2) The v3 comment says the revision changed the argument, so v1 and v3 may not carry the same Parshin claims; I read only the ar5iv rendering. (3) I found no reviewer, citing paper or verification specific to the Parshin cases.
events.direction: Cuts in the conjecture's direction, but only for the listed restricted families and for stacks of low dimension; it does not address the general statement.

events.what_happened: Bruno Kahn, arXiv:math/0205158, first posted 14 May 2002 as 'Equivalence rationnelle, equivalence numerique et produits de courbes elliptiques sur un corps fini' (v2, 20 Jul 2002, extends the main results to smooth projective varieties of 'abelian type' under the Tate conjecture and corrects errors of v1). Published as 'Equivalences rationnelle et numerique sur certaines varietes de type abelien sur un corps fini', Ann. Sci. ENS (4) 36 (2003) 977-1002. Abstract: for X of abelian type over a finite field satisfying the Tate conjecture, rational and numerical equivalence agree. Parshin's conjecture is not named in the abstract. The consequence for Parshin's conjecture (for abelian-type varieties of dimension at most 3, combined with Soule's result that such varieties satisfy Tate in dimension at most 3) is attributed to Kahn, Corollaire 2.2, in Gregory (2023), and a search summary says P follows for abelian type using Geisser and Kimura. I did not open the Annales text.
events.revisions: v1 14 May 2002 (products of elliptic curves); v2 20 Jul 2002 (abelian type; corrected errors of v1). The v2 abelian-type claim may be the first version carrying the Parshin consequence; not verified.
events.delivers: Parshin's conjecture for smooth projective X of abelian type over F_q: conditionally on the Tate conjecture for X (Kahn's main theorem, with Geisser and Kimura), and unconditionally for abelian-type X of dimension <= 3 (Kahn Corollaire 2.2, as cited by Gregory). These are restricted classes (abelian type: products of curves, abelian varieties, Fermat-type varieties and similar).
events.remains: P for smooth projective varieties of dimension >= 4 and for all varieties not of abelian type; also the conditional cases where Tate fails or is unknown.

checked_by.who: Annales scientifiques de l'Ecole Normale Superieure (editorial and referee process)
checked_by.what_they_did: published the paper (vol. 36, 2003, pp. 977-1002); refereeing not inspected
checked_by.where: https://arxiv.org/abs/math/0205158 (journal details from a search result; the journal page itself was not opened)

events.doubts: The Parshin consequence is stated in secondary sources (Gregory 2023 citing Kahn Cor 2.2) and was not verified in Kahn's text. The abstract of v2 does not mention Parshin.
events.direction: Cuts in the conjecture's direction for the restricted class of abelian-type varieties (dimension <= 3 unconditionally, all dimensions conditionally on Tate).

events.what_happened: Thomas Geisser, 'Tate's conjecture, algebraic cycles and rational K-theory in characteristic p', K-Theory 13 (1998) 109-122. Characterises Tate's conjecture via motives and the Frobenius endomorphism. Shows: if Tate's conjecture holds and rational and numerical equivalence agree over finite fields, then the higher rational K-groups of smooth projective varieties over finite fields vanish (Parshin's conjecture; Theorem 1.2 per a search summary, Theorem 3.3 cited by Gregory as [Gei98]). Also notes that Parshin's conjecture implies a Beilinson-Kahn bound conjecture. Known only from search snippets and secondary citations; the journal copy was not opened.
events.delivers: Conditional: P for smooth projective varieties over finite fields satisfying Tate's conjecture and the agreement of rational and numerical equivalence.
events.remains: Unconditional P; and P for any variety not known to satisfy both hypotheses.

checked_by.what_they_did: published the paper (1998); refereeing not inspected

events.doubts: Conditional result; the hypotheses are not known to hold for the general case. Journal copy not read by me.
events.direction: Reduction: conditional support for the conjecture under two hypotheses; does not settle it.

events.what_happened: Thomas Geisser, 'Parshin's conjecture revisited', arXiv:math/0701630 (v1 23 Jan 2007; v2 21 May 2008), published in EMS volume 'Algebraic K-Theory and Noncommutative Geometry' (Valladolid 2006 proceedings), Ser. ECR 60 (2008), pp. 413-425, DOI 10.4171/060-1/13. Restates P as vanishing of rational higher Chow groups CH_n(X,i) tensor Q for i > 0 (Conjecture P(n) for all n), and, assuming resolution of singularities, splits P(n) into three conjectures A(n), B(n), C(n). The EMS page was opened; the arXiv record was seen only in search snippets.
events.revisions: v1 23 Jan 2007; v2 21 May 2008 (per search snippet).
events.delivers: A reformulation: P is equivalent to P(n) for all n; under resolution of singularities P(n) is equivalent to A(n) and B(n) and C(n). It establishes no new case of P by itself.
events.remains: All of P: the three split conjectures A(n), B(n), C(n) are themselves open.
events.doubts: None on the record; the paper is a reformulation.
events.direction: Neutral: a reformulation that leaves the conjecture open; no object.

events.what_happened: Thomas Geisser, 'Parshin's conjecture and motivic cohomology with compact support', arXiv:1002.0105 (posted February 2010; exact day not checked), later published in Comment. Math. Univ. Sancti Pauli 64 (2015), no. 2, 95-107. Studies implications of P for motivic cohomology with compact support (using the dual groups H^i_c(X,Q(n))^*) and relates bounds for four rational motivic theories to P. Not opened; seen in search snippets only.
events.revisions: arXiv v1 Feb 2010; journal version 2015 (not opened).
events.delivers: Consequences of P for motivic cohomology with compact support; relates bounds to P. Does not settle P or any case of it, on the snippets I saw.
events.doubts: Not read in full by me.
events.direction: Neutral implications of the conjecture; no object.

events.what_happened: Daniel Quillen, 'On the cohomology and K-theory of the general linear groups over a finite field', Ann. of Math. 96 (1972). Computes the higher K-groups of finite fields, which are finite. Via Wikipedia and Barwick-Nardin (2018) this is the dimension-0 case of P. Not opened directly; cited in the Wikipedia article (opened) and in Barwick-Nardin (opened).
events.delivers: Dimension 0: for smooth projective zero-dimensional X over a finite field (finite extensions of F_q), K_i(X) is finite for i >= 1, so P holds. This settles dimension 0 entirely.
events.remains: P for all X of dimension >= 1.
events.direction: Consistent with the conjecture; settles the dimension-0 case.

events.what_happened: Gunter Harder, 'Die Kohomologie S-arithmetischer Gruppen uber Funktionenkorpern', Invent. Math. (1977). Per the Wikipedia article (opened) and Barwick-Nardin (opened), Harder's Corollary 3.2.3 gives the dimension-1 case: higher K-groups of smooth projective curves over finite fields are torsion. Grayson (1982) gives finite generation. Not opened directly.
events.delivers: Dimension 1: for smooth projective curves over finite fields, the higher K-groups are torsion, so P holds for curves. This settles dimension 1 entirely.
events.remains: P for all X of dimension >= 2.
events.direction: Consistent with the conjecture; settles the dimension-1 case.

events.what_happened: Clark Barwick and Denis Nardin, 'A comment on the vanishing of rational motivic Borel-Moore homology', arXiv:1811.07656 (v1 19 Nov 2018; v2 22 Nov 2018). Abstract (opened): a weak form of Parshin's conjecture, on the vanishing of rational motivic Borel-Moore homology of quasi-projective varieties over finite fields in a range of bidegrees, holds if and only if the cyclic action on the motivic cohomology of an Artin-Schreier extension is trivial in the relevant bidegrees. The comment says v1 was 'too strong' as pointed out by Joseph Ayoub, and v2 corrects it. The paper also notes the m = 0 case (Quillen) and m = 1 case (Harder).
events.revisions: v1 19 Nov 2018 (too strong, per the comment); v2 22 Nov 2018 (corrected).
events.delivers: A reduction: the weak form of P (Borel-Moore homology vanishing in a range) is equivalent to a cyclic-action triviality statement on motivic cohomology of Artin-Schreier extensions. It does not prove the weak form, nor P.
events.remains: The weak form of P and the full conjecture, both reduced to the cyclic-action statement.
events.doubts: The comment records one human correction (Joseph Ayoub, of an earlier formulation). The v2 formulation's proof was not read by me beyond the abstract and introduction.
events.direction: Reduction of a weak form of the conjecture to a cyclic-action statement; no counterexample.
people: Joseph Ayoub (acknowledged, for the v1 correction)

events.what_happened: Oliver Gregory, 'Motivic cohomology and algebraic K-theory of some surfaces over finite fields', arXiv:2302.09867 (v1 20 Feb 2023; v2 17 Aug 2023; no journal reference). Computes motivic cohomology and K-theory of some classes of surfaces over finite fields via the motivic Atiyah-Hirzebruch spectral sequence. Introduction (Remark 1.1, opened): 'Parshin's conjecture remains wide open, but there are some partial results.' The appendix shows P for surfaces admitting a rational decomposition of the diagonal (Corollary A.3, stated over the algebraic closure of F_q) and states that P holds for K3 surfaces of geometric Picard rank 20 ('singular K3 surfaces'). Gregory says the known cases (unirational surfaces, abelian surfaces, singular K3 surfaces) make the K-group computations unconditional. Acknowledged support: EPSRC grant EP/T005351/1 and the Heilbronn Institute for Mathematical Research.
events.revisions: v1 20 Feb 2023; v2 17 Aug 2023 (current per the arXiv abstract page). No journal reference listed.
events.delivers: P for surfaces admitting a rational decomposition of the diagonal (over the algebraic closure of F_q), and for K3 surfaces of geometric Picard rank 20; enlarges the class of surfaces where P is known. Restricted to surfaces.
events.remains: P for all smooth projective varieties of dimension >= 3, and for surfaces outside the listed classes; the paper states the conjecture remains wide open.
events.doubts: None identified in the source. The appendix's proofs were read only in part.
events.direction: Partial support for the conjecture in restricted surface classes; the paper says the general conjecture is open.

events.what_happened: Finn Bartsch and Ariyan Javanpeykar, 'Parshin's method and the geometric Bombieri-Lang conjecture', arXiv:2407.10706 (15 Jul 2024). A survey explaining Parshin's proof of the geometric Bombieri-Lang conjecture, and an alternative proof of Xie and Yuan's result for certain projective varieties. Different Parshin (a namesake).
events.delivers: Nothing toward P. It concerns the geometric Bombieri-Lang conjecture and does not concern K-theory of varieties over finite fields.
events.direction: Not bearing on this conjecture (namesake).

events.what_happened: F. Deglise, 'Generic motives and motivic cohomology of fields', arXiv:2408.06233 (12 Aug 2024). Studies generic motives and motivic cohomology of fields; proposes a conjecture complementing the Beilinson-Soule vanishing conjecture. Does not mention Parshin or finite fields in the abstract (opened). A search snippet says that for fields of characteristic p > 0 the Beilinson-Soule-type statement follows from two well-known conjectures; not verified in the text.
events.delivers: Nothing toward P on the abstract. It is a neighbouring statement (Beilinson-Soule vanishing for fields), not Parshin's conjecture.
events.direction: Not bearing on this conjecture (neighbouring problem).

events.what_happened: Matt Broe, 'On the Beilinson-Bloch conjecture over function fields', arXiv:2505.00696 (v1 1 May 2025; v2 27 Jan 2026). Gives a criterion for Beilinson-Bloch over global function fields; a new proof of a theorem of Geisser linking the Tate conjecture over finite fields with Birch and Swinnerton-Dyer over function fields; and Tate for a product of a curve with a power of a CM elliptic curve over finitely generated fields. Parshin is not mentioned (opened).
events.delivers: Nothing toward P. Neighbouring Tate and Beilinson-Bloch results over function fields.
events.direction: Not bearing on this conjecture (neighbouring problem).

events.what_happened: Rahul Gupta, Amalendu Krishna, Jitendra Rathore, 'Motivic Cohomology and K-groups of varieties over higher local fields', arXiv:2603.21000 (v1 22 Mar 2026). Proves that K-groups of quasi-projective varieties over higher local fields are divisible-by-finite above a suitable degree, and finiteness of prime-to-p torsion in certain higher Chow groups of smooth projective varieties. The abstract (opened) does not mention Parshin, Beilinson or Tate, and concerns higher local fields rather than finite fields.
events.revisions: v1 22 Mar 2026; later versions not checked.
events.delivers: Nothing toward P as stated: the results concern higher local fields, not finite fields. The divisible-by-finite conclusion is adjacent to P's finiteness-plus-torsion shape.
events.direction: Not bearing on this conjecture (different fields).

disputes.summary: Yousefzadehfard's arXiv v1 (Nov 2020) says 'We prove the Parshin's conjecture'; the author then withdrew v2 with the comment 'There is a problem with the Theorem 4.7.' Gregory's 2023 preprint says the conjecture 'remains wide open' and does not cite the 2020 preprint. The record does not resolve which is right; I have not weighed it.

Tabuada's arXiv (2017, v3 2018) lists Parshin's conjecture among the conjectures proved in new cases over finite fields. The published JNCG version (2023) has an abstract mentioning only the Tate conjecture and its variants, so whether the Parshin cases appear in print is unresolved.

summary: Parshin's conjecture (the higher algebraic K-groups of smooth projective varieties over finite fields vanish up to torsion, i.e. rationally) has no accepted resolution on the sources I could reach as of 13 Oct 2026. The events I found fall into four groups. (1) The only claimed full proof: arXiv:2011.05544, Yousefzadehfard, v1 11 Nov 2020, which says 'We prove the Parshin's conjecture'. The author withdrew v2 on 21 Nov 2020 and the arXiv record carries the comment 'There is a problem with the Theorem 4.7.' The v1 PDF body could not be read by my tools (the download is a compressed stream and ar5iv returned nothing), so I could not check the argument, or whether Theorem 4.7 is one of its steps. No journal publication, refutation, review or citing paper was found, and Gregory's 2023 bibliography does not cite it. This is pre-window, so under the rule for dating the first written argument it is a 2020 event. (2) Restricted-class results: Kahn (arXiv 2002, Annales ENS 2003) for abelian-type varieties, with dimension <= 3 unconditional via Soule, and Tabuada (arXiv Dec 2017) for determinantal linear sections, Segre varieties, S_{1,1,2}, some quadric intersections and low-dimensional stacks; and Gregory (arXiv Feb 2023, rev Aug 2023) for surfaces admitting a rational decomposition of the diagonal and singular K3 surfaces of Picard rank 20. Gregory's introduction says the conjecture 'remains wide open'. (3) Conditional and reduction results: Geisser 1998 (Tate plus rational=numerical), Geisser 2007/2008 (split into A(n), B(n), C(n)), Geisser 2010/2015 (motivic cohomology with compact support), and Barwick-Nardin 2018 (weak form equivalent to a cyclic-action statement). The classical dimension-0 (Quillen 1972) and dimension-1 (Harder 1977) cases are settled. (4) Things in the window (after 26 Jan 2024) that touch the field but not the problem: Bartsch-Javanpeykar 2024 (a different Parshin, on Bombieri-Lang), Deglise 2024 (generic motives, Beilinson-Soule), Broe 2025 (Beilinson-Bloch over function fields, not Parshin), and Gupta-Krishna-Rathore 2026 (higher local fields, no Parshin mention). None of these bears on the conjecture, so in the window the status is that I found no event moving it. Close calls: whether the 2020 v1 claim should count as a resolution, given the author's own flag and the later 'wide open' statement, is for the judging pass; whether Tabuada's and Kahn's restricted families count as cases is also for that pass, and whether Tabuada's Parshin cases were kept in print is unresolved. AI: no source on this problem names an AI system. The 2020 preprint's abstract, listing, and withdrawal note say nothing about tools, and its body could not be read, so AI involvement in its body is unverified. Explicit AI searches (AI labs, Erdos and FrontierMath trackers, 'AI proof' wording) returned only unrelated results: the May 2026 OpenAI disproof of the unit-distance conjecture, a GPT-5.5 Pro sum-product disproof, the Tsoukalas et al. formal-proof-search paper (arXiv:2605.22763, which names no problem and does not mention Parshin or K-theory), and a FrontierMath item on del Pezzo surfaces that is not about K-theory. An Epoch footnote about a Jacobian-conjecture counterexample is unrelated. The Wikipedia article (fetched via a summary tool) has no status section and names only dimensions 0 and 1 as known cases; the summary tool is not a full read.
competing_reading: If the 2020 v1 argument is correct, the conjecture was settled by a human author in November 2020. That would be a pre-window event, and the window would then show only a withdrawn duplicate, not new mathematics. The case against this reading is the author's own withdrawal of v2 with the note that Theorem 4.7 is flawed, the absence of any accepted version or expert verification, and the 2023 Gregory preprint calling the conjecture 'wide open' without citing the claim. Gregory's silence is weak evidence (the claim may simply have been ignored), not a rejection. Conversely, a reader who weighted the withdrawal lightly could read Tabuada's and Kahn's restricted results as cases, while a stricter reader would say the general statement is untouched by any of them.
what_would_settle_it: (a) A readable copy of arXiv:2011.05544 v1, to see whether Theorem 4.7 carries the main argument and whether the flawed step is fatal. (b) A published or refereed version of 2011.05544, or an expert note or MathSciNet/zbMATH review of it. (c) A 2024-2026 paper that cites 2011.05544 as correct or as flawed. (d) The author's own later statement on the claim. (e) For Tabuada, the published JNCG text, to see whether the Beilinson and Parshin cases are in print. (f) For the restricted results, a statement from the judging pass on whether the listed classes count as cases of the conjecture as frozen.

judgement.why: All events bearing on the conjecture predate 26 January 2024. The only whole-claim (Yousefzadehfard 2020) is knocked down by the author's own withdrawal flagging Theorem 4.7, with no later version. Quillen, Harder, Kahn, Tabuada and Gregory settle restricted classes (dimensions 0 and 1, abelian type in dim <= 3, specific families, certain surfaces), so they are cases; journal publication counts as digestion for the classical papers and Kahn, while Tabuada's Parshin content is doubtful in print and Gregory is an unrefereed preprint. Geisser's papers and Barwick-Nardin are conditional reductions/reformulations, scope none. The four post-snapshot events concern a namesake or neighbouring problems (Bombieri-Lang, Beilinson-Soule for fields, Beilinson-Bloch, higher local fields) and are variants. No AI system appears anywhere.
judgement.doubts: Kahn's Parshin consequence and the Geisser papers rest on secondary citations, not on the texts read. Quillen and Harder have no checked_by entries but are classical published results; marked digested on that basis. Post-snapshot rows could arguably be 'none' rather than 'variant'; either is discarded.
